profile.title: The Language of Networks: An Introduction to IEEE 802.3 and 802.11 Standards
profile.subject: Academic Course Material
profile.mainTopic: The Language of Networks: An Introduction to IEEE 802.3 and 802.11 Standards

topics.name: IEEE 802.3 and IEEE 802.11 Standards
topics.description: Introduces the IEEE standards associated with wired Ethernet and wireless local area networking.

topics.name: Ethernet as a LAN Technology
topics.description: Defines Ethernet as a widely used local area network technology for communication among connected devices.

topics.name: Wired Ethernet
topics.description: Explains wired Ethernet as a network in which devices are physically connected through networking media and interface hardware.

topics.name: Introduction to Ethernet
topics.description: Establishes the scope of IEEE 802.3 and IEEE 802.11 and introduces Ethernet networking.

topics.name: Wired Network Interface Card
topics.description: Presents the wired Network Interface Card as the device interface that enables a computer to connect to an Ethernet network.

topics.name: Wireless Network Interface Card
topics.description: Presents the wireless Network Interface Card as the interface that enables a device to communicate over a wireless network.

topics.name: Network Interface Hardware
topics.description: Identifies the interface cards used to connect devices to wired and wireless networks.

topics.name: IEEE 802 Communication Rules
topics.description: Describes standardization as the establishment of common rules that allow heterogeneous devices to communicate with one another.

topics.name: IEEE Standardization
topics.description: Explains how standardized rules enable communication between different network devices.

topics.name: Ethernet (802.3) Wired LAN
topics.description: Presents IEEE 802.3 as the standard underlying wired local area networks and their physical network communication.

topics.name: Ethernet Receiver Synchronization and Destination Identification
topics.description: Explains how Ethernet communication supports receiver synchronization and uses a destination MAC address to identify the intended receiver.

topics.name: CSMA/CD
topics.description: Describes Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection as the method used to coordinate transmissions and manage traffic on shared wired Ethernet.

topics.name: Ethernet Communication and Medium Access
topics.description: Explains the functions of IEEE 802.3 Ethernet communication and the CSMA/CD access method.

topics.name: Evolution of Ethernet
topics.description: Traces the progression from Standard Ethernet in the 1980s to Fast Ethernet, Gigabit Ethernet, and systems operating at 10 Gbps and beyond.

topics.name: Classification of Ethernet Networks
topics.description: Classifies Ethernet networks into four types according to their generation and supported data-transfer rate.

topics.name: Fast Ethernet (802.3u)
topics.description: Defines Fast Ethernet as the IEEE 802.3u generation that raised Ethernet performance to 100 Mbps, ten times the original Ethernet rate.

topics.name: Auto-negotiation
topics.description: Explains auto-negotiation as a Fast Ethernet and newer Ethernet feature through which connected interfaces determine mutually supported communication settings.

topics.name: Gigabit Ethernet (802.3ab)
topics.description: Introduces Gigabit Ethernet as a 1000 Mbps standard used to support modern high-speed local area networks.

topics.name: Ethernet Generations and Speeds
topics.description: Traces Ethernet development from Standard Ethernet through faster generations and examines their principal characteristics.

topics.name: Fiber-Optic and Copper UTP Media
topics.description: Compares fiber-optic and copper UTP as Ethernet media, including infrastructure cost and deployment considerations.

topics.name: Ethernet Cable Types
topics.description: Surveys the various cable designations used for Ethernet implementations, including 10Base2 and other media-specific Ethernet cable types.

topics.name: Ethernet Transmission Media
topics.description: Compares Ethernet media and surveys cable types used by different Ethernet implementations.

topics.name: IEEE 802.11 Wireless LAN Standard
topics.description: Introduces IEEE 802.11 as the standard for wireless LAN communication and relates it to wireless networking methods, media, and user benefits.

topics.name: 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz Wireless Bands
topics.description: Compares the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands in terms of range, speed, crowding, and susceptibility to interference.

topics.name: Wireless LAN Standards and Radio Bands
topics.description: Presents IEEE 802.11 wireless networking and compares the operating characteristics of common frequency bands.

topics.name: CSMA/CA Wireless Medium Access
topics.description: Explains how a wireless device listens to the medium before transmitting and uses collision avoidance to reduce competing transmissions.

topics.name: Wireless Network Components
topics.description: Identifies the access point, station, and SSID, including the access point's role as a bridge between wired and wireless networking.

topics.name: Wireless Access and Components
topics.description: Explains how wireless devices access the shared medium and identifies the central elements of a wireless network.

topics.name: Wired (802.3) versus Wireless (802.11) Connectivity
topics.description: Compares wired Ethernet and wireless LAN connectivity to determine which standard best fits particular infrastructure needs.

topics.name: Wired and Wireless Infrastructure
topics.description: Evaluates the selection of IEEE 802.3 or IEEE 802.11 according to infrastructure requirements.

topics.name: Wi-Fi 7, Terabit Ethernet, and IoT Integration
topics.description: Highlights Wi-Fi 7, Terabit Ethernet, and Internet of Things integration as developments aimed at higher throughput and broader connectivity.

topics.name: Future of Network Connectivity
topics.description: Introduces technologies expected to advance network capacity and integration.

topics.name: Shared Ethernet Transmission
topics.description: Examines a shared Ethernet cable scenario in which only one computer can transmit at a time, reinforcing shared-medium access behavior.

topics.name: Upgrade from Standard Ethernet to Fast Ethernet
topics.description: Assesses an upgrade from 10 Mbps Ethernet to 100 Mbps Fast Ethernet while retaining existing network cabling.

topics.name: Ethernet Access and Upgrade Scenarios
topics.description: Applies Ethernet principles to shared-medium communication and network upgrades.

topics.name: Settings Negotiated by Ethernet Interfaces
topics.description: Reviews the communication parameters selected by a Fast Ethernet Network Interface Card through auto-negotiation.

topics.name: Mutually Supported Ethernet Speed
topics.description: Applies auto-negotiation to a 1 Gbps laptop connected to a switch that supports only 100 Mbps.

topics.name: Gigabit Ethernet Media Support
topics.description: Reviews the capability of Gigabit Ethernet to operate over supported copper or fiber media rather than requiring only one medium.

topics.name: Auto-negotiation and Gigabit Ethernet Review
topics.description: Assesses negotiated Ethernet settings, compatibility between different link speeds, and Gigabit Ethernet media support.

topics.name: Why Wi-Fi Uses CSMA/CA
topics.description: Reviews the use of CSMA/CA in Wi-Fi because wireless devices cannot reliably detect collisions while transmitting.

topics.name: Ethernet and Wireless LAN Comparison
topics.description: Assesses the distinction between Ethernet and wireless LAN operation, particularly their different medium-access methods.

topics.name: Wireless Access and Standards Comparison Review
topics.description: Assesses why wireless LANs use collision avoidance and how their operation differs from wired Ethernet.
